title: Activepieces vs Integrately: 2026 Comparison Guide
summary: Activepieces vs Integrately: One offers self-hosted infrastructure with an MIT-licensed core. You'll see which suits your automation control requirements.
body_markdown:
## Integrately judged on every criterion


Integrately is a hosted, template-first product: you pick a ready-made automation and switch it on instead of building the flow yourself.


That suits a marketing or operations team with no developer, because setup is choosing and connecting rather than designing.


You work inside the vendor's hosted service, and that is the trade-off. I found no self-hosting option in its pricing page or docs, so teams with data-residency or on-premises requirements should ask Integrately directly.


### Integrately pricing and task limits


The bill follows how often your automations run, not how many you build, because Integrately meters by tasks.


Integrately's pricing page lists $19.99 a month, billed annually, for 2,000 tasks and $239 a month, billed annually, for 150,000, so you need to estimate your monthly usage to select the right plan.


Divide each price by its task count. The unit economics appear: roughly 2.45 cents per task at the first tier, 2.49 cents at the second, and 0.4 cents at the third.


Moving from 2,000 to 10,000 tasks multiplies volume by five and the price by just over five, so the second tier buys no discount.


At 150,000 tasks you pay about six times less per task than at 10,000, and that is where the economics change.


Before you pick a tier, count how many tasks one run of your busiest automation consumes, because a multi-step flow can use several.


### Integrately admin, AI and embedding features


On SSO, admin controls, AI agent capabilities or embedding Integrately inside your own product, the pricing page, docs and changelog give me no published detail I can quote. I won't guess at them.


If any of these is a requirement, ask Integrately in writing and get the answer tied to a named plan, because a feature that exists on one tier may not exist on the $19.99 one.


### Where the hosted route is the better buy


Integrately's design removes the work that makes open source costly for a team without a developer. Nobody patches a server, schedules backups or answers an uptime alert, and the person who sets up an automation is the person who needs it.


On the criteria above, that wins on hosting effort and on time to a first working flow. It also gives a simple spending model when your needs match its templates: a plan fee tied to task volume, with no infrastructure line beside it.


A small team running common app-to-app jobs, such as moving form leads into a CRM, may never meet the limits that push others toward open source.


If that describes you, the control Activepieces offers is something you would carry without using, and Integrately is the sensible purchase.
